What this document does not do
It does not write leaderboard scores or rankings.
Scores change with the version, the aggregation method and the model list, and copying them makes them go stale quickly. Read them on the official site or in the paper,

The values measured directly in this repository are in “What we saw in this data” in each module README. The “This repository” column below points to that location. Those values are results of small models, few seeds and one dataset, so they
cannot be compared with the official scores of the benchmarks
The “what cannot be said” column of the tables is the author’s judgment (not a claim of the paper).
7 questions before using a benchmark (a summary of module 06 §6)

children.label: 7 questions before using a benchmark (a summary of module 06 §6)

children.value: What is the origin of the labels? Is it an experiment, a human annotation, or an annotation transferred from sequence similarity (a leakage path)?
What leakage does the split block, and what does it fail to block?
Did you measure the overlap in numbers after splitting?
Is the metric suited to the task? Is it a single average, or is it by type and with uncertainty?
Are simple baselines (one that learns no parameters, simple features, random initialization) included with the same procedure?
Can the pretraining data and the evaluation data overlap? Did you check?
If you keep looking at the same test and choosing models, you get fitted to the test. Is there a hidden test/version pinning?
Are the data version and the license stated?
Do self-supervised protein embeddings transfer to downstream tasks?
semi-supervised tasks from different areas of protein biology (abstract). The train/val/test split was fixed per task to look at “biologically meaningful generalization” (abstract)
The split differs per task. You must check the split definition you will use for each task
The ranking of modern large PLMs (a 2019 benchmark, centered on the models of that time)
for protein engineering work even in low-data and extrapolation conditions?

Experimental data on AAV stability, GB1 stability and immunoglobulin binding, and the thermostability of several families (abstract). Low-data and extrapolation generalization settings are deliberately included
which split a score was read under
Sequence-based protein understanding overall (function, localization, structure, interaction, ligand) and multi-task learning

17 tasks in 5 categories (web-search summary): function prediction, subcellular localization, structure, protein–protein interaction, protein–ligand interaction (abstract). Compares feature engineering, sequence encoders and large PLMs, and also surveys multi-task learning
With many tasks, collapsing to a single average erases the per-task differences
DMS fitness prediction at the scale of ProteinGym, design (whether any of the PEER tasks are variant-data-based is to be checked in the paper’s tables†)

More than 250 standardized DMS assays (millions of variant sequences) and clinically annotated data, zero-shot and supervised settings, a comparison of more than 70 models (abstract). The v1.3 substitution file of this repository has 217 assays. Per-assay Spearman is used

If other substitutions at the same position are in train, a model that has learned the position effect has an advantage. The DMS target proteins may be in the pretraining corpus. The official aggregation is per-type aggregation, so it
differs from the simple average of the notebook

The DMS fitness score alone cannot say anything about the ability of clinical pathogenicity prediction (the clinical subset is a separate evaluation target, and this repository did not use it. The goal differs)

An evaluation study — reports that current models do not explain inter-individual expression variation well
Between-gene differences of the reference genome ≠ the personal cis-variant effect

Quantitative evaluation of data integration (batch correction)
A collection of metrics that measure batch mixing and biological conservation together (ASW, etc.)
Do not be fooled by a method that is high on only one metric. Check the consistency between metrics
The downstream predictive ability of a model
Evaluates scGPT and Geneformer without fine-tuning, and reports that they can fall behind simple methods (abstract)
The evaluation data may be in the pretraining corpus

Compares 5 FMs and 2 deep-learning models with deliberately simple baselines, and reports that none exceeded the baseline in predicting the transcriptome change after single and double gene perturbations (abstract)
The definition of the split of the perturbation data (new perturbation vs new cell)
Not a model but an evaluation tool
A continuously updated single-cell benchmark such as OpenProblems was not checked in this repository (⚠️ 미검증 (unverified)).
A collection of molecular property prediction
Several property datasets (this repository uses 3 small ones: ESOL, Lipophilicity, BBBP)

Even with the scaffold split, a considerable share of the test molecules are very similar to train (module 05: 26% of the Lipophilicity test at Tanimoto ≥ 0.7). The original source and license of each dataset need checking
Generalization to a new chemical space
ML data and tasks across all stages of therapeutic development
22 learning tasks, 66 datasets (web-search summary). NeurIPS 2021 Datasets & Benchmarks. Reports that even the best algorithms show limits under distribution shift and so on
Check the split definition per task
Do pretrained molecular embeddings exceed ECFP?
28 models, 25 classification datasets. Reports that, except for one model (CheMeleon), none exceeded the ECFP count fingerprint (abstract, preprint)
A preprint, depends on the settings
Are pathology FMs robust to differences between medical centers?
Reports that all 10 public pathology FMs strongly represent the medical-center signal (abstract, preprint)
Weights such as UNI/CONCH need access approval. This repository did not use them
More than 2,400 multiple-choice questions (literature, figure interpretation, database navigation, DNA/protein sequence manipulation, etc.; abstract). A public subset is provided on HF

When reading a new benchmark (a 3-minute check)

children.label: When reading a new benchmark (a 3-minute check)

children.value: You did not take at face value the abstract’s “best on our data”. Check whether the setting selection was done on the test set
You wrote the split rule in one line, and wrote the paths that cannot be blocked
. If not, add it yourself (module 07 checklist)
You looked at both the average score and the per-type/per-task scores
You pinned the version (the leaderboard of an official site may be updated)
